title: Clouds that make stars
question: What is a nebula and what does it do?
hook: A nebula can be hundreds of light-years wide, yet an Earth-sized piece of one weighs only a few kilograms.
idea: Nebulae are thin clouds of gas and dust where material can clump together until it becomes dense enough to form stars.

beats.prompt: Inside a nebula, gas and dust clump into a denser patch. What happens as the patch keeps growing?

choices.label: It drifts apart again
choices.feedback: A denser patch pulls in more matter rather than losing it.

choices.label: It attracts more matter and may form a star
It stops at the size of a planet
choices.feedback: Growth does not stop there; the patch can become dense enough to form stars, and the leftover material forms planets.

beats.explain: The clumps attract further matter and eventually become dense enough to form stars; the remaining material is thought to form planets.

beats.prompt: Put these nebula discoveries in order, oldest first.
items: Christiaan Huygens makes the first detailed study of the Orion Nebula (1659)
Edmond Halley publishes a list of six nebulae (1715)
Charles Messier compiles a catalog of 103 "nebulae" (by 1781)
Edwin Hubble announces that nearly all nebulae are associated with stars (1922)
beats.explain: Huygens studied Orion in 1659, Halley listed six nebulae in 1715, Messier had 103 by 1781, and Hubble made his announcement in 1922.

beats.prompt: Match each astronomer to what they found.
pairs: About a third of the nebulae he examined had a gas's emission spectrum
The nebula around Merope shines by reflected starlight
Nearly all nebulae are associated with stars
The first true nebula distinct from a star cluster
beats.explain: Each of these astronomers added a piece to our picture of what nebulae are.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning is wrong. Which?
steps: A nebula is a cloud of gas and dust in the interstellar medium.
Some nebulae are hundreds of light-years across.
So a nebula must be denser than any vacuum made on Earth.
Even so, an Earth-sized piece would hold only a few kilograms.
beats.explain: Most nebulae are far less dense than any vacuum created on Earth.
